reason: The draft answers Marisol's question directly and correctly: skip the 22, because three weeks out it would add fatigue she can't shed before October 18. It backs that up by pointing to the 20 and the 17 she has already run. Next week adds up to about 45 mi (6+9+8+4+18), a small step from 42 and in line with the 53 peak. The 18-mile long run, with the last 4 at marathon pace, is a sensible last long run three weeks out. It follows the 17 and is shorter than the earlier 20, so it isn't a jump. The plan keeps her five days with Mon/Fri off, a Wednesday session and a Sunday long run. The 8:30–8:40 reps are close to her 3:45 goal pace (about 8:35/mi), and every day can be run as written, with paces and heart-rate caps. Nothing on the card calls for a must-never check: no pain, illness, fatigue or return from a break. I took off a point because the draft never speaks to the anxiety she mentioned about the new date. It also doesn't say how the next two weeks will taper, which would have reassured someone worried about less time.
